You drive a fist into the sentry’s jaw, and he staggers but stays upright. Before you can pull back, he shoves forward and clamps his pilum-hand into your space, pinning you against the gate’s timber strut with brutal leverage.

He wrenches you off the strut with a sharp twist, keeps you pinned by the shoulder, and brings his gladius in tight, the blade angled at your throat with the point steady. “You hit a man on duty,” he barks. “Stay down, or I end it.”
